FILE q_ods.wav:
ods01 (0.0-9.9s): "Brain cells adapt to low sodium by shedding osmolytes. A rapid rise in sodium then pulls water out of them, and the myelin breaks down."
ods02 (11.4-17.0s): "The central pons is hit hardest, where grey and white matter are tightly interwoven."
ods03 (18.5-30.5s): "Symptoms are delayed, usually two to six days after the correction. Slurred speech, trouble swallowing, weakness in all four limbs, and in severe cases, locked-in syndrome."
ods04 (32.0-39.9s): "On MRI, diffusion restriction comes first, within about a day. T2 and FLAIR changes can lag by up to two weeks."
ods05 (41.4-49.9s): "On axial T2, look for a bright central pons shaped like a trident. The outer rim of the pons and the corticospinal tracts are spared."
ods06 (51.4-58.1s): "It can also strike outside the pons. Look for symmetric signal in the basal ganglia and thalami."
ods07 (59.6-67.0s): "Risk is highest with alcohol use disorder, malnutrition, liver disease, and low potassium."
ods08 (68.5-78.7s): "Prevention is the treatment. In chronic hyponatremia, guidelines limit correction to about eight to ten millimoles per litre in any twenty-four hours."
ods09 (80.2-86.2s): "Recently corrected sodium, and a trident in the pons? Think osmotic demyelination."
Key words: osmotic demyelination (dee-MY-uh-lin-AY-shun); osmolytes (OZ-mo-lites); pons (PONZ); hyponatremia (high-po-nuh-TREE-mee-uh); thalami (THAL-uh-my); corticospinal

FILE q_hod1.wav:
hod00 (0.0-7.4s): "Hypertrophic olivary degeneration is a rare case where a damaged structure gets bigger, not smaller."
hod01 (8.9-20.2s): "It starts with a circuit called the Guillain-Mollaret triangle. It links the red nucleus in the midbrain, the inferior olive in the medulla, and the dentate nucleus in the opposite cerebellum."
hod02 (21.7-32.2s): "The dentate sends fibres up through the superior cerebellar peduncle, crossing to the red nucleus. The red nucleus connects down to the olive through the central tegmental tract."
hod03 (33.7-40.4s): "A bleed, an infarct, or surgery that interrupts this pathway leaves the olive without its input."
hod04 (41.9-46.0s): "Its neurons swell and vacuolate, so the olive enlarges."
Key words: olivary (OL-ih-vair-ee); Guillain-Mollaret (ghee-YAN moh-luh-RAY); dentate (DEN-tate); tegmental (teg-MEN-tul); peduncle (peh-DUNK-ul or PEE-dunk-ul); vacuolate; palatal (PAL-uh-tul); medulla

FILE q_hod2.wav:
hod05 (0.0-10.1s): "On MRI, the olive in the front of the medulla turns bright on T2 about a month after the injury. It enlarges at around six months, and it does not enhance."
hod06 (11.6-17.9s): "Years later the swelling settles and the olive shrinks, but the bright signal can persist."
hod07 (19.4-28.5s): "Which side? A lesion in the central tegmental tract affects the olive on the same side. A cerebellar lesion affects the opposite olive."
hod08 (30.0-35.7s): "The classic clinical sign is palatal tremor, a rhythmic movement of the soft palate."
hod09 (37.2-43.2s): "A bright, enlarged olive, with an old lesion in the triangle? Don't call it a tumour."
Key words: olivary (OL-ih-vair-ee); Guillain-Mollaret (ghee-YAN moh-luh-RAY); dentate (DEN-tate); tegmental (teg-MEN-tul); peduncle (peh-DUNK-ul or PEE-dunk-ul); vacuolate; palatal (PAL-uh-tul); medulla

FILE q_bun.wav:
bun00 (0.0-6.9s): "Two parkinsonian syndromes, two classic MRI signs. The hot cross bun, and the hummingbird."
bun01 (8.4-17.5s): "Multiple system atrophy combines parkinsonism, cerebellar ataxia, and autonomic failure, like fainting on standing and bladder problems."
bun02 (19.0-27.8s): "In the cerebellar type, the transverse fibres of the pons and the midline raphe degenerate, while the corticospinal tracts are spared."
bun03 (29.3-34.0s): "On axial T2, that leaves a bright cross in the pons. The hot cross bun sign. The pons and cerebellum also shrink."
bun04 (35.5-45.5s): "It isn't specific. Some spinocerebellar ataxias show it too."
bun05 (47.0-51.5s): "Progressive supranuclear palsy causes early falls, usually backwards, a stiff neck and trunk, and a vertical gaze palsy, especially looking down."
bun06 (53.0-60.8s): "Here the midbrain shrinks, but the pons stays plump."
bun07 (62.3-67.3s): "On the midline sagittal view, the thin midbrain forms the head and beak, and the pons forms the body. That's the hummingbird sign."
bun08 (68.8-76.7s): "On axial images, the same midbrain atrophy gives the Mickey Mouse appearance."
bun09 (78.2-84.8s): "A cross in the pons, think multiple system atrophy. A hummingbird midbrain, think progressive supranuclear palsy."
Key words: atrophy; ataxia; raphe (RAY-fee); pons; spinocerebellar; supranuclear; sagittal (SAJ-ih-tul)
